questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What is the name for an error or fault in a computer program?
questions.explanation: A fault in a program is called a bug. Fixing bugs is called debugging.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
options: Adding new features to a program
Finding and fixing errors in a program
questions.answer: Finding and fixing errors in a program
questions.hint: The opposite of putting bugs in.
questions.explanation: Debugging means tracking down errors (bugs) in a program and fixing them so the program behaves correctly.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: A program runs but gives the wrong answer. What kind of error is this most likely to be?
questions.hint: The program works — it just thinks the wrong thing.
questions.explanation: A logic error means the program runs without crashing but produces the wrong result. The instructions don't match what the programmer intended.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: A program won't even run because the programmer typed 'pritn' instead of 'print'. What kind of error is this?
questions.hint: It's a mistake in the rules of the language.
questions.explanation: A syntax error breaks the rules of the language — the computer can't understand the instruction and refuses to run the program.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which of these are sensible debugging strategies? (Select all that apply.)
options: Add print statements to check variable values
Run the program with test data and compare to expected results
Delete the program and start again every time
Step through the code line by line
answer: Add print statements to check variable values
Run the program with test data and compare to expected results
Step through the code line by line
questions.hint: Deleting everything isn't really debugging — it's surrender.
questions.explanation: Good debugging means investigating: read errors, print values, step through, and test against expected outputs. Just deleting and starting again loses progress and doesn't teach you what was wrong.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Why do programmers test their programs with different kinds of input?
options: To check the program behaves correctly in different situations
To make it harder for users
questions.answer: To check the program behaves correctly in different situations
questions.hint: Testing is about catching problems before users find them.
questions.explanation: Different inputs reveal different bugs. Testing helps prove the program works for normal, unusual, and even invalid data.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: A program accepts ages from 0 to 120. Which is an example of BOUNDARY test data?
questions.hint: Boundary data is right on the edge of what's allowed.
questions.explanation: Boundary data sits on the limits of what's allowed. 0 and 120 are boundary values. 55 is normal, 'Banana' is invalid, and -50 is out of range.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: A program accepts ages from 0 to 120. Which is an example of INVALID test data?
questions.hint: Invalid means the program should refuse to accept it.
questions.explanation: 'Banana' isn't even a number, so a well-written age program should reject it. Invalid data tests that the program handles bad input safely.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
options: Writing the whole program in one go and never changing it
Building, testing and improving the program in repeated cycles
Letting the computer write the code
questions.answer: Building, testing and improving the program in repeated cycles
questions.hint: Iterate means to repeat — the same idea as in loops.
questions.explanation: Iterative development means building a small piece, testing it, getting feedback, then improving — repeating that cycle until the program is finished.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: What does 'requirements analysis' mean at the start of a project?
options: Working out exactly what the program needs to do, and for whom
Deciding what colour the buttons will be
questions.answer: Working out exactly what the program needs to do, and for whom
questions.hint: Before you build anything, you need to know what's being asked for.
questions.explanation: Requirements analysis is the first stage of a project: clarify what the user needs and what the finished program must do. Without it, you risk building the wrong thing.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Why is it useful to write down clear requirements before you start coding?
options: So you can evaluate at the end whether the program meets the user's needs
So the file size is smaller
So you don't have to test
questions.answer: So you can evaluate at the end whether the program meets the user's needs
questions.hint: Without requirements, how would you judge 'done'?
questions.explanation: Clear, written requirements give you something to evaluate against. You can check, at the end, whether each requirement is met.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: In Python, which symbol starts a comment that the interpreter ignores?
questions.explanation: In Python, anything after a # on a line is a comment and is ignored by the interpreter. Comments are for human readers only.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Why do programmers add comments to their code?
options: To make the program run faster
To explain what the code does, for themselves and other developers to read later
questions.answer: To explain what the code does, for themselves and other developers to read later
questions.hint: Comments are for the humans, not the machine.
questions.explanation: Comments explain why and how code works. They help future readers (including you in six months) understand the program quickly.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Which of these are good documentation habits in a program? (Select all that apply.)
options: Using clear variable names like 'score' instead of 'x'
Adding comments to explain tricky logic
Writing one giant unlabelled block of code
Removing all whitespace to save space
answer: Using clear variable names like 'score' instead of 'x'
Adding comments to explain tricky logic
questions.hint: Clarity beats cleverness — code should read like a story.
questions.explanation: Good naming, helpful comments, and small named functions all make code easier to understand. Removing whitespace or making giant blocks does the opposite.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: Put the stages of a typical project lifecycle in the correct order.
questions.hint: Understand it, plan it, build it, test it, judge it.
questions.explanation: A typical lifecycle: analyse requirements first, design the approach, implement (code) it, test against those requirements, then evaluate and improve. The cycle usually repeats — that's iterative development.

further_learning.title: Introduction to Python Programming – Oak National Academy
KS3 Computing – BBC Bitesize

questions.subject: computing
questions.prompt: You are testing a quiz program. You want to make sure it handles every type of input safely. Which set of test cases is most thorough?
options: Only inputs that the program already passes
questions.hint: Real users do weird things — your tests should too.
questions.explanation: Thorough testing covers normal data (typical use), boundary data (edges of what's allowed) and invalid data (rubbish input). That combination catches the most bugs.
